plan.notes: Source: official BYU 'BS in Computer Science (693220) MAP Sheet' for students entering during the 2024-2025 curricular year, published by the BYU College of Physical and Mathematical Sciences (these MAP documents are the same Major Academic Plans the University Catalog stores under its Major Academic Plans (MAPs) section). Source URL: https://science.byu.edu/00000191-9a7e-d806-afb1-be7f718f0001/3-map-bs-in-computer-science-2024-2025-pdf (2024-2025 is the newest CS MAP published; no 2025-2026 or 2026-2027 MAP exists as of 2026-09-30). Degree name verified from the MAP title: 'BS in Computer Science'. Transcription method: manual verbatim transcription of the MAP's 'Suggested Sequence of Courses' (8 semesters) from the PDF text. CAVEATS: (1) The MAP prints Minimum hours needed to graduate = 120.0, but its own suggested-sequence term totals sum to 121.0-122.0 (14.50 + 16.00-17.00 + 14.50 + 15.00 + 14.00 + 16.00 + 16.00 + 15.00); total_credits=121 follows the sequence's own total (Clarkson/UVM precedent) - the extra 1-2 hours are open electives. (2) Spring Year 1 is transcribed exactly as the MAP prints it: 'American Heritage or First Year Writing' 4.0 and 'University elective' 1.0 - these values are internally consistent with the MAP's printed term total of 16.00-17.00. (3) The 3.0-credit path (MATH 290 or STAT 220) is used for the Spring Y1 math choice; choosing MATH 113 (4.0) raises that term to 17.0 and the plan total to 122. (4) Prereqs are intentionally left empty - the MAP gives a suggested order but not per-course prerequisite lists; students use MyMAP / their advisement center. (5) The four 'Religion Cornerstone course' slots and five 'GE Arts, Letters, and Sciences' slots are student-choice slots with distinct placeholder codes; options are verbatim from the MAP. (6) MAP Requirement 5 = 21.0 hours of electives: five slots are pinned to Option 5.1 (12-21 hours from the listed CS courses); the two Spring Y4 'CS Elective' slots may come from any of options 5.1-5.4. (7) CS 191 (0.5) and CS 291 (0.5) are 0.5-credit courses as printed. (8) catalog.byu.edu's MAP index page was unreachable (transient upstream timeout) at collection time; the PDF above is the official BYU-published MAP document.
